record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let T1, ..., Tℓ be arbitrary invertible measure-preserving transformations, not assumed to commute, and let p1, ..., pℓ be distinct integer polynomials with zero constant term. For every measurable set A with positive measure, must there exist m, n ∈ N such that μ(A ∩ T1^{m+p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{m+pℓ(n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Let (X, X , µ) be a probability space, T1, . . . , T` : X → X be invertible measure preserving transformations, and p1, . . . , p` be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Show that for every A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0 we have µ(A ∩ T1^(m+p1(n))A ∩ · · · ∩ T`^(m+p`(n))A) > 0 for some m, n ∈ N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell\colon X\to X$ be invertible measure-preserving transformations (no commutativity is assumed). Let $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[n]$ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Prove or disprove: for every $A\in\mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A)>0$ there exist $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{m+p_1(n)}A\cap T_2^{m+p_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{m+p_\ell(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved in the special case where the polynomials $p_1,\dots,p_\ell$ are rationally independent (Chu–Frantzikinakis–Host type result, 2013), using reductions to nilfactors and equidistribution on nilmanifolds. Further progress on multiple recurrence and convergence for non-commuting transformations along iterates $m+p_i(n)$ was made by Frantzikinakis (J. London Math. Soc., 2023). The full statement for arbitrary distinct integer polynomials with zero constant term does not appear to have a published resolution.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence for non-commuting transformations along polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: We prove a multiple recurrence result for arbitrary measure-preserving transformations along polynomials in two variables of the form m+p_i(n), with rationally independent p_i's with zero constant term.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the problem under the additional hypothesis of rational independence of the polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence and convergence without commutativity
status_evidence.snippet: Frantzikinakis, J. London Math. Soc., 2023, on multiple recurrence and convergence without commutativity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent progress on the non-commuting case, but the general distinct-polynomial form of the problem is not stated as fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including the stated polynomial recurrence problem without commutativity.
